1037.text: You have destroyed the opponent's army!

1044.text: You have captured the river fort!

1070.text: Your combined army has destroyed the opponent!

1045.text: Your opponent has captured the river fort!

1048.text: Your opponent has captured the town!

1051.text: Your opponent has taken the hill!

1054.text: Your opponent has captured Twinbridge Keep!

1061.text: Your conquest of the castle has failed!

1062.text: You have lost the castle to your opponent!

1067.text: Your conquest of the town has failed!

1068.text: You have lost the town to your opponent!

1071.text: Your combined army has been destroyed!

796.text: Perhaps your days as a squire have not yet prepared you for war. I shall have to think on this.

798.text: We shall reach the imperial city by tomorrow, squire. Tonight we will treat the men to meat and wine in the village ahead.

799.text: What is this now? Looters fleeing the coming war?

801.text: Captain Morro. See to the wounded villagers and set our camp for the night.

805.text: Wake up, squire. The day is upon us and the men need to be assembled.

808.text: The men are ready then? Good.

810.text: You have quality within you. I've always seen that. Fight well today and a knighthood shall be yours.

811.text: Our Emperor is young, but cautious.

814.text: We have crossbowmen and catapults well placed on the ridge. We should let the enemy come to us while we rain rock and arrow down upon their heads.

815.text: As their army closes with ours, try to position the cavalry in line for a charge. With our foot soldiers... ATTACK AT WILL!

816.text: Flank and surround the enemy units to deliver more damage with each melee attack! Break holes in their line to weaken their formation defense!

817.text: Sweep around their position! Close in and finish them!

818.text: Your valor today does you credit PlayerName, as does the years of your service to my family.

823.text: Our western division is under attack! How would you have us assemble, Sir PlayerName?

824.text: Sir! Should we fight through to their catapults, or flank their front line and crush them between our combined forces?

825.text: The western front is secure, but the enemy has struck with their reserves at the heart of our battle line. The Emperor is in danger!

827.text: Our eastern division has been completely shattered! Duke Pellus leads his vanguard at our Emperor! We must reach him before he is overrun!

828.text: Capture the boy alive if possible! Cut down the rest!

829.text: Duke Pellus has been defeated! Long live the Emperor!

831.text: The Emperor has fallen. All hope for the Empire is lost.

832.text: The enemy is broken! We've won!

838.text: Greetings, PlayerStyle PlayerName. It is good to see you safe and well through the Merovin Rebellion.

841.text: Men of Carrone! Today you will learn to fight as soldiers of the Third Legion!

847.text: In facing a reinforced position, such as this fortress, war engines are critical in bringing down the walls or gate!

844.text: In defending a reinforced position, such as this fortress, use ranged attacks from the shelter of towers or ramparts to weaken the approaching army!

850.text: I take pride knowing that I trained you as squire. Your skill in battle will return the Empire to its former glory!

851.text: You are a worthy adversary, PlayerStyle PlayerName. Any further assistance in training the Legion would be met with my deepest gratitude.

852.text: Merovin infantry approach along the river, supported by cavalry traveling the ridgeline.

854.text: The Baron's men are defeated and our scouts report the valley clear to the bridge keep ahead.

856.text: The guard at the bridge keep has been reinforced, but our reserves have arrived as well.

858.text: We have secured the bridge crossing!

860.text: Baron Valeuve approaches to treat with you before the battle, PlayerStyle.

865.text: Men of Valeuve, grant no quarter! Advance and destroy the enemy of Merovin!

866.text: Fight on, men! Do not lose heart! Drive them back to their Emperor!

867.text: I am forced to deliver my surrender. Valeuve is yours, PlayerStyle.

869.text: Gather your men, sergeant! Hold them here for as long as possible!

870.text: East a half day's march sits Castle Corbeau, PlayerStyle.

872.text: Numerous though they were, they could not hope to stop us.

874.text: PlayerStyle, the enemy has dug a picket line and brought up musketeer and cannon support from the castle.

876.text: Militia advance! Keep them at cannon range!

877.text: We've broken through their line and captured their cannon!

879.text: The town of Corbeau is just south of the castle, PlayerStyle.

881.text: Fools! They may have taken the barbican, but they will break themselves upon the walls of my castle!

882.text: Yield! I yield! Grant me safe passage from Corbeau and the castle is yours!

884.text: Towns such as these cover the foothills of Bordavia and provide trade into the region.

886.text: The town guard was expecting our arrival, PlayerStyle.

888.text: Count Valamir's vanguard approaches from the east, PlayerStyle PlayerName!

890.text: Their vanguard has been shattered, but our scouts report the rest of Count Valamir's host waits for some reason.

892.text: Count Valamir's army has arrived, PlayerStyle.

895.text: Men of Carrone. Bordavia is open to you no longer. Surrender this town and return to your own country...

897.text: May the gods curse each day you spend within my country.

898.text: Their assault has broken itself upon our defenses, PlayerStyle.

901.text: The main body of your army has yet to make their landing at Whitecliff, PlayerStyle.

906.text: We're losing men! If half of our number are lost, we'll not reach Stokeshire!

907.text: The men are dying, PlayerStyle PlayerName! Should we lose any more, we're done for!

908.text: We've escaped their trap, but the enemy gathers for pursuit.

910.text: We've lost too many men to have hope of reaching Stokeshire. We must turn back.

911.text: We've gained the high ground! They will pay dearly if they mount an assault upon this position.

915.text: I hope that we have not been delayed too long to aid Castle Stokeshire.

916.text: The men are exhausted. We have no chance of reaching the castle.

918.text: May devils take you, Martin! To think I once called you brother! Now I name you kinslayer!

922.text: PlayerStyle PlayerName! The castle is nearly done for!

924.text: Keep at it, lads! The bailey is ours and the keep is ripe to fall!

925.text: Where are those cursed trebuchets? That gate should be rubble by now!

926.text: I yield. Spare my men and the castle is yours, Martin.

930.text: RETREAT! Through the hunting gate and into the wood! Stokeshire must wait for now.

935.text: Brother! I have captured your imperial envoy!

939.text: Your army has been well provisioned by the Carrone camp and awaits your marching orders.

947.text: Conquer the gate as quickly as possible. The longer we fight here the more of their damned griffon riders will descend upon us.

948.text: With the losses you have suffered, we must retreat and assemble a stronger force.

949.text: Well done, PlayerStyle PlayerName. Lead the vanguard into the pass and the legion shall follow for the siege upon El Acclazar.

950.text: The Third Legion's war engines will take time to gain the summit of the pass.

955.text: A war engine has been lost! If we lose two more, continuing forward will be futile!

956.text: A second war engine destroyed! We can not afford to lose a third if we hope to siege El Acclazar!

957.text: Too many war engines have been destroyed. We must retreat to the Third Legion's camp.

961.text: The war engines of the Third Legion are in position and reserve infantry will march forward after your advance.

965.text: All of the reserves are now committed to the field. Lead us to victory, PlayerStyle PlayerName.

966.text: El Acclazar has fallen! You have conquered where all others have failed! It is an honor to serve in your army, PlayerStyle.

968.text: PlayerStyle PlayerName, we must retreat. With our losses, we cannot hope to conquer the fortress, much less hold it against any counter attack. El Acclazar must wait for another day.

969.text: This village is too close to our coastal shipyards and would be a natural launching point for Hunewold raids.

972.text: Spirits of their ancestors rise up to fight alongside their shamans!

974.text: The men are disquieted by the forest, PlayerStyle PlayerName, but I shall oversee its clearing at once for the fortress timbers.

976.text: Hunewold tribesmen approach from all sides, PlayerStyle PlayerName.

979.text: PlayerStyle PlayerName. It appears that three different tribes are part of this attack.

981.text: The tribesmen host has broken and their survivors scatter into the wood to carry the tune of their defeat.

983.text: PlayerStyle PlayerName, I come with word just delivered from our far watch patrol.

987.text: By the gods! The very trees sway with the stamp of their approach!

989.text: Victory! VICTORY! Hail PlayerName, blessed be his name!

994.text: Our first casualty! We must break through or finish the enemy before our numbers diminish!

995.text: We're losing too many men! If more than half of the troops are slain, the supplies are lost!

996.text: The supplies are in danger! Should we lose any more men, we're finished!

998.text: The supplies will be seen safely through to your fort, PlayerStyle PlayerName.

997.text: The raiders have captured our supplies!

999.text: You have the Emperor's trust and favor, PlayerStyle PlayerName.

1003.text: Setting fire to these huts will draw their scouts to investigate.

1005.text: Two days since our attack upon their camp and still no counter from the Horselords.

1007.text: PlayerStyle PlayerName! Horselords riding hard from the west!

1008.text: REGROUP! They seek to strike at the rear flanks of our column!

1009.text: The size of their force was smaller than expected. This could not have been their full strength.

1011.text: The Horselords have arrived in strength, PlayerStyle PlayerName. Our scouts estimate they have nearly twice our number.

1016.text: By the grace of the Emperor...!

1017.text: And for the glory of Carrone!

1018.text: My Lord, your Grace, when no word arrived of your landing we feared the worst.

1023.text: A Horselord column has ridden in from the east!

1024.text: A second column now, to the west!
